question.problem:
Find all real eigenvalues of the matrix 
$A=[\begin{aligned}-4 & 2 \\ 6 & 7\end{aligned}].$
question.worked_solution:
Let's start by writing the matrix $A-\lambda I:$
﻿﻿﻿

$$
A-\lambda I=[\begin{aligned}-4-\lambda  & 2 \\ 6 & 7-\lambda \end{aligned}]
$$

Now, let's find and solve the characteristic equation $det(A-\lambda I)=0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}det(A-\lambda I) & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}-4-\lambda  & 2 \\ 6 & 7-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (-4-\lambda )(7-\lambda )-2\cdot 6 & =0 \\ -28-7\lambda +4\lambda +{\lambda }^{2}-12 & =0 \\ {\lambda }^{2}-3\lambda -40 & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Using the quadratic formula, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\lambda  & =\frac{3\pm \sqrt{(-3)^{2}+4\cdot 1\cdot 40}}{2} \\  & =\frac{3\pm \sqrt{169}}{2} \\  & =\frac{3\pm 13}{2} \\  & =8,-5.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the eigenvalues are $\lambda =8$ and $\lambda =-5.$
